disposition_reason: Reports cadmium, lead, arsenic, copper and zinc by AAS in three leafy vegetables bought at five rural and urban markets in Kwara State, Nigeria.

study.origin: not stated (sellers interviewed about farm source)
study.market: Ilorin, Ajase-Ipo, Oke-Onigbin, Oro and Omu-Aran markets, Kwara State, Nigeria
study.method: washed, oven-dried 75 C, dry ashed 550 C, 2 N HCl, AAS (AOAC 2000)
study.qa: no CRM, recovery or blank reported; LSD0.05 printed per column

findings.group: vegetable section of Ilorin market, Kwara State
findings.notes: market leaves bought from five randomly selected sellers; washed, oven-dried at 75 C and milled; tables do not state dry or fresh basis; single value per location (no SD); AAS after dry ashing

unresolved: Abstract arsenic range (0.08-0.17) differs from the tables (0.09-0.18); flagged on all arsenic findings.
Abstract ranges for lead (0.06-0.13), copper (0.09-0.18) and zinc (0.05-0.16) do not match the tables for copper and zinc; table values used.
The printed calculation "Heavy metals (mg/kg) = Titre value x volume used / Molar mass of HCl" does not describe an AAS calculation.
Text says copper and zinc "for all the locations" were 0.05-0.06 and 0.08-0.10 mg/kg, which matches only amaranth (Table 2).
Nitrate and nitrite are not metals and not recorded; dry or fresh basis not stated.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: FAO/WHO (2010) limits as printed in Tables 1-3
regulatory_or_exposure.value: Cd 0.2, Pb 0.3, As 0.2, Cu 40, Zn 99.4 mg/kg; nitrate 3.7, nitrite 0.07 mg/kg
